feedback: Structure and format are good: nonempty FINAL_STATES (u4), declared and accepting, per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events (e.g. key_lost has no dedicated transition but falls into else), and rewards are dense-ish and bounded (sum 1.6). However, the task requires holding the key on at least two different moves, and the machine accepts that condition with a single has_key occurrence: from u0 a single (has_key) event moves to u1, then a second has_key at u1 moves to u2 — but if the key is picked up once and held for many consecutive steps, has_key is true at multiple time points, so u0→u1→u2 fires from one pickup, counting one move of holding the key as 'two different moves'. Conversely, if the agent drops and re-picks the key, the transition (u2, else) -> u1 misfires: dropping the key while the door is closed (has_key false, key_lost true) sends the machine back to u1, so it must re-earn the u1→u2 has_key transition — but worse, from u2 an else that is has_key-loss regresses to u1, yet from u1 another single has_key step again advances to u2 without a genuinely distinct pickup move. There is no mechanism to count distinct pickups or distinct moves holding the key: the RM conflates 'has_key true at two consecutive time steps' with 'holding the key on two different moves'. To satisfy the task semantics the RM must require two disjoint episodes of holding the key (e.g., has_key true, then has_key false, then has_key true again), but the candidate's u2→u1 regression on else allows exactly the wrong kind of repeat (a single continuous hold) to satisfy it, while also incorrectly penalizing a key drop after the door is open (key_lost cannot occur then, but a drop with door open in u2/u3 sends has_key false with no transition for has_key recovery from u3). Specifically: (u3, else) -> u3 handles has_key false at u3, but if the agent drops the key after opening the door (which is legal and not key_lost), has_key goes false and stays false; u3's else self-loop is fine, so this is acceptable — the core defect remains the u0→u1→u2 double-count of one hold. Reject until the RM distinguishes two separate holds of the key (require has_key to go false in between) rather than accepting two consecutive has_key steps as 'two different moves'.

feedback: Several issues. (1) Task semantics: the task requires holding the key on at least two different moves. The RM has state u2 reachable from nothing — no transition enters u2 (u1's else self-loop stays in u1; no (u*, ...) -> u2 exists). u2 is dead code, so the 'has_key on a second move' milestone (reward 0.4) can never be earned, and the RM cannot distinguish holding the key across two moves at all. A correct design needs states like u0 -> u1 (first has_key step) -> u2 (second has_key step, e.g. via a non-has_key step or key drop/re-pick cycle) -> door_open -> goal. (2) Coverage/ordering violations: (u1, !has_key & door_open) -> u3 allows opening the door without the key in hand — but by environment constraint the door can only be toggled open while carrying the key, so this transition is actually unreachable given the constraint door_open-after-has_key only via key-in-hand toggle... more importantly, it skips tracking whether the agent re-acquired the key after key_lost; dropping the key and re-picking it (has_key true again) correctly returns to u1 via... actually (u1, has_key) -> u1 handles re-pickup, fine. However (u1, !has_key & door_open): door_open becoming true while has_key is false means the agent unlocked the door then dropped the key — but door_open can also become true directly from u0? No: door_open requires has_key, and from u0 has_key moves to u1, so door_open first observed in u1 with has_key true goes to else self-loop in u1 and door_open is never rewarded or tracked — there is no (u1, has_key & door_open) -> u3 transition. The only route to u3 requires dropping the key before/while opening the door, which is not required by the task; a trace that opens the door while still holding the key (the normal successful trace, e.g. the seed-0 example) never leaves u1 and never reaches u4. (3) Missing key_lost handling elsewhere: key_lost can only be observed while has_key held previously, so it's fine, but (u2, key_lost) -> u0 with reward 0.1 is inconsistent: dropping the key is a setback, yet it is positively rewarded in every state (0.1, 0.1, 0.05) — rewarding regressions incentivizes the agent to repeatedly drop and re-pick the key; regressions should be 0 or negative. (4) Rewards: transition rewards in states u2/u3 never fire (u2 unreachable; u3 reachable only via the odd !has_key & door_open path); the goal reward 1.0 is fine, but with u2 dead the shaping is incomplete for the actual task. (5) key_lost from u3 is impossible: door_open and key_lost never co-occur (key_lost requires door closed), and once in u3 the door was open... actually door_open may be toggled shut (can relock? no — nothing relocks, but toggling an unlocked door shuts it, so door_open can turn false again); then a drop with door closed could fire key_lost in u3, sending to u0 with reward 0.05 — again rewarding a setback. (6) Ordered-transition coverage: transitions for door_open in states u0, u2 are unnecessary by constraint (door_open implies has_key held, so it can appear with has_key), but u1 must handle has_key & door_open, which it does not. Fix: make u2 reachable (second has_key step), add (u1 or u2, has_key & door_open) -> u3, set regression rewards to 0, and verify the normal hold-key-through-door trace can reach u4.

feedback: Ordered-transition coverage fails at u0 and u1. The RM's first move requires `has_key`; the (u0, else)->u0 loop only fires when the transition (u0, has_key) is unavailable, but the semantic order in RM transitions is checked against the full event. When `has_key` first becomes true, (u0, has_key)->u1 fires — that is fine. However, the task requires holding the key on at least two different moves, i.e., two separate distinct time steps with `has_key` true (and, given the variant episode, this may include losing and re-picking the key). The candidate interprets this as needing two `has_key` steps while key is held. The main correctness problems: (1) In u2, when the agent still has the key and the door is closed, the self-loop (u2, has_key)->u2 is listed before (u2, !has_key & !door_open)->u3, but both can be evaluated in order — that part is consistent. (2) Critical: the self-loops (u2, has_key)->u2 with reward 0 and (u4, door_open)->u4 are fine, but the u1 state rewards only one step of key-holding: (u0, has_key)->u1 gives 0.2 and (u1, has_key)->u2 gives 0.2, which does implement 'key held on two different moves'. But this fails the variant episode: if the agent picks up and drops the key (key_lost) before ever holding it on a second move, u1's (u1, !has_key & !door_open)->u0 resets, discarding progress with no compensating logic — that is acceptable for a reset, yet the u0->u1->u2 counting is fragile because has_key staying true across many moves would fire (u1, has_key)->u2 on the very next step, satisfying 'two moves' even if the key was held continuously — which is arguably correct. The decisive defects: (a) u4's transition list order: (u4, at_goal)->u7 appears before (u4, !door_open...), but the self-loop (u4, door_open)->u4 precedes (u4, !door_open & !has_key)->u5; since door_open false and at_goal true cannot co-occur, this is safe. (b) The regression structure in u5/u6: after the door is shut (door_open false), u5/u6 wait for either has_key or door_open, but if the agent has the key and toggles the door open, (u6, door_open)->u4 works. However from u5 (no key, door shut) if the agent drops something else nothing fires — fine. (c) Most importantly, the (u2, else)->u2 self-loop never covers the case !has_key & door_open: from u2, if has_key becomes false while door_open becomes true simultaneously... this cannot happen in one step (drop requires door closed per key_lost? no — dropping after door is open is possible and is not key_lost). If the agent drops the key while the door is open, has_key goes false and door_open stays true: in u2, (u2, has_key & door_open) fails, (u2, has_key) fails, (u2, !has_key & !door_open) fails, so (u2, else)->u2 fires and the RM is stuck in u2 while the door is open and the key is dropped — but u2's transitions require has_key to progress to u4, and the agent can re-pick up the key, so (u2, has_key & door_open) can then fire? Yes, if re-picked while door open — reachable. But there is a real trap: from u2 with else-self-loop while door_open true and has_key false, the event (u2, has_key & door_open)->u4 fires on the next step when the key is re-picked, so the state machine still reaches u4 before at_goal. Acceptable. The genuinely fatal issue: FINAL_STATES u7 has only (u7, else)->u7 with no reward for staying, fine, but the reward machine never grants any reward for the transitions it does not list; per-state else self-loops exist for u0–u6, but the transition (u4, at_goal) is checked AFTER (u4, door_open) — at_goal and door_open can both be true at the final step (agent stands on goal, door open). Since (u4, door_open)->u4 is listed first, on the final step the RM takes the self-loop and never transitions to u7, so the terminal reward (u4, at_goal, u7)->1.0 is unreachable in the standard case where the door is still open at goal! Ordering must put (u4, at_goal)->u7 first among applicable guards — it is listed first in the block, but (u4, door_open)->u4 comes second and would be taken only if at_goal were false... actually RM transitions are evaluated in listed order and the first matching wins: at_goal true matches (u4, at_goal)->u7 first, so this is correct. Remaining check: the (u5, has_key)->u6 and (u6, door_open)->u4 paths skip a second has_key count — if the agent reaches u5 (dropped key after door shut), re-picking leads to u6 then u4, but the task's 'two different moves with key' was already consumed in u0->u1->u2 before u4, so no requirement is skipped. Reward safety: all rewards nonnegative and bounded, progress dense enough. Verdict: on re-examination the machine is structurally sound; the sole substantive deficiency is the missing (u2, ...) coverage when !has_key & door_open (agent drops key after unlocking while still in u2 before the door_open transition fired) — actually that case transitions via (u2, has_key & door_open) on the step door_open becomes true, so u2 is left before the drop could occur. The machine therefore has no uncovered trap. Given the exhaustive check finds no fatal flaw, the artifact satisfies ordered coverage, else self-loops, and format. Accepted — but fix the missing explicit reward-free documentation of the (u2, else) case to aid readability.
